newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Jan 9.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BUSINESS PANEL HITS AT TORIES ON COMPETITION

A group of senior businessmen and academics is set to publish a report criticising the government's record on promoting competition. The group, the Commission on Public Policy and British Business, was set up almost two years ago under the auspices of the left-wing Institute for Public Policy Research. The report also lends some support to introducing the Social Chapter in Britain, and suggests that a minimum wage could have benefits for "good employers".
-- HALIFAX SET TO PAY AVERAGE OF 1,300 STG IN SHARES

The Halifax, the world's biggest building society, is expected to announce on Friday that its 8.5 million members could receive windfall share bonuses worth an average of about 1,300 stg. A pay-out of that amount would top the 1,233 stg average due to Woolwich members later this year, and values the Halifax at about 11 billion stg - making it one of Britian's top 20 companies by market capitalisation.
-- LLOYDS FINED 325,000 STG FOR PENSION SELLING

Lloyds Bank, part of the Lloyds TSB group, has become the first bank to be punished over the selling of personal pensions. City watchdog Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) has fined Lloyds a record 325,000 sterling over the issue. Investigations into the sale of personal pensions in the late 1980s and early 1990s -- in particular, advising people to switch from group or company schemes to personal pensions -- were launched industry-wide in late 1994.
-- REUTERS IN LEGAL DISPUTE WITH HEALTH MINISTER

Information group Reuters is involved in a dispute with the Department of Health over a new, computerised prescription system. Ministers have refused to sanction the Healthplus system, which is to be marketed by the Reuters subsidiary VAMP, after fears that it raises questions about patient confidentiality. The VAMP system is intended to allow doctors to use computers to transfer prescriptions to pharmacists, saving time and cutting administration.
-- BRUSSELS SET TO BACK COCA COLA DEAL

The European Commission is expected to approve the 1.2 billion stg sale by Cadbury Schweppes and Coca-Cola of their British bottling joint venture to Coca-Cola Enterprises . A decision, which is not likely to involve any special conditions, is expected before the end of the month. The deal will give Coca- Cola Enterprises full control of Coca-Cola & Schweppes Beverages, and is likely to be cleared after a panel of national experts recommended it despite local objections from smaller competitors.
-- TELECOMMUNICATIONS GROUP TO LOSE 20 PERCENT OF ITS STAFF

Humberside-based telecoms operator Kingston Communications, Britain's only municipally-owned telecommunications company, is to shed up to 20 percent of its staff. Kingston said up to 300 of its 1,530 staff would be made redundant in a "fundamental restructuring of the business to enable it to perform more effectively in the intensely competitive telecommunications market."
-- WATER INDUSTRY PLEDGES TO IMPROVE SERVICE

The Water Services Association, the body representing the nine biggest water and sewerage companies in England and Wales, has launched an unprecedented campaign to improve its public image. The WSA has set out a range of goals, including commitments to the environment and to "the best level of service of any utility." The launch was marked by an acknowledgement that the companies had got their priorities wrong in some areas, particularly over leaks.
-- EX-ENERGY MINISTER EGGAR TO TAKE JOB AT OIL GROUP

Former energy minister Tim Eggar is set to join the board of Monument Oil and Gas as a non-executive director. The appointment, which has been cleared by the parliamentary watchdog on business appointments, is expected to renew the political controversy over former ministers taking jobs in industries they have overseen.
-- BMW TO PRODUCE IMPROVED EARNINGS

Bernd Pischetsrieder, chairman of German automotive group BMW, said he expects group earnings in 1996 to be above the DM692 million (263 million stg) generated after tax in 1995. The prediction, made in an interview with the Financial Times newspaper, comes despite continuing heavy losses at BMW's British subsidiary Rover. He said that Rover would lose less than it did in 1995, and that the present strength of sterling would have no significant effect on Rover's results.
-- DIXONS' PROFITS UP BUT SHARES FALL

Electrical retailer Dixons has reported a 53 percent increase in interim pre-tax profits to 57.5 million stg. Sales for the period rose 24 percent to 1.06 billion stg. Despite the results, shares in the group fell 5 percent, largely due to profit-taking. The market is also reported to be uncertain about the effects of an increase in tax payable on extended product warranties.
